```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 9,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 150,
  out.width = "100%"
)

# Load existing project scripts
source("Packages.R")
source("data.R")

# Consistent colors
red  <- "#EF4444"
blue <- "#3B82F6"
grey <- "#64748B"

# Helper functions
fmt_pct <- function(n, total) {
  ifelse(total > 0,
         sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * n / total),
         "NA")
}

fmt_median <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  if (length(x) == 0) return("NA")

  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))

  sprintf("%.2f [%.2f, %.2f]",
          q[2], q[1], q[3])
}

# Check required variables
required_vars <- c(
  "PatientID",
  "AKI_any",
  "AKI_any_early",
  "AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case",
  "Protein_intake__d1_4",
  "days_onexclusive_oral_feeding",
  "died_in_ICU",
  "EuroScore2",
  "BMI",
  "Duration_of_cardiopulmonary_bypass_minutes",
  "SBP"
)

missing_vars <- setdiff(required_vars, names(data))

if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing columns: ",
    paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Validate binary outcome coding
outcome_vars <- c(
  "AKI_any",
  "AKI_any_early",
  "AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case"
)

for (v in outcome_vars) {
  values <- unique(as.numeric(data[[v]]))
  values <- values[!is.na(values)]

  if (!all(values %in% c(0, 1))) {
    stop("Invalid binary coding in: ", v)
  }
}

# Create local analysis dataframe
eda <- data %>%
  transmute(
    PatientID,

    AKI_primary = as.numeric(AKI_any),
    AKI_day56 = as.numeric(AKI_any_early),
    AKI_worst = as.numeric(AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case),

    Protein = as.numeric(Protein_intake__d1_4),
    Oral_days = as.numeric(days_onexclusive_oral_feeding),

    ICU_death = case_when(
      as.character(died_in_ICU) == "Yes" ~ 1L,
      as.character(died_in_ICU) == "No" ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    ),

    EuroScore2,
    BMI,
    CPB = Duration_of_cardiopulmonary_bypass_minutes,
    SBP
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Protein_group = factor(
      case_when(
        Protein == 0 ~ "Zero",
        Protein > 0 ~ "Positive",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("Zero", "Positive")
    )
  )

# Verify that day 5-6 AKI is nested within primary AKI
nesting_errors <- sum(
  eda$AKI_day56 == 1 & eda$AKI_primary == 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

late_AKI_valid <- nesting_errors == 0

# Derive AKI after day 6 only if nesting is consistent
eda <- eda %>%
  mutate(
    AKI_after6 = case_when(
      !late_AKI_valid ~ NA_integer_,
      is.na(AKI_primary) | is.na(AKI_day56) ~ NA_integer_,
      AKI_primary == 1 & AKI_day56 == 0 ~ 1L,
      AKI_primary == 1 & AKI_day56 == 1 ~ 0L,
      AKI_primary == 0 & AKI_day56 == 0 ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  )

# Outcome labels
outcome_labels <- c(
  AKI_primary = "AKI after day 4",
  AKI_day56   = "AKI on days 5-6",
  AKI_after6  = "AKI after day 6",
  AKI_worst   = "Worst-case AKI"
)
```

# Study Overview

## Research Question

Is artificially administered protein intake during the first four ICU days associated with subsequent acute kidney injury (AKI) in patients undergoing major cardiac surgery?

This project is a post-hoc observational analysis of a subgroup of the SUSTAIN CSX trial. Artificial protein administration was determined by the treating physician and was not randomized.

## Study Outcomes

| Outcome | Variable | Definition |
|---|---|---|
| Primary | `AKI_any` | New AKI after ICU day 4 until ICU discharge or death |
| Secondary | `AKI_any_early` | New AKI on ICU days 5-6 |
| Exploratory | Derived from primary and secondary outcomes | AKI after ICU day 6, if derivation is valid |
| Sensitivity | `AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case` | Patients dying without documented AKI are classified as AKI cases |

The mapping of the first two variables follows the team's previous checks against the original modified AKI columns.

# Study Population and AKI Frequencies

```{r study-summary}
study_summary <- eda %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    ICU_deaths = sum(ICU_death == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Zero_protein = sum(Protein == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    Positive_protein = sum(Protein > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

knitr::kable(
  study_summary,
  caption = "Overview of the study population"
)

outcomes_to_show <- c(
  "AKI_primary", "AKI_day56", "AKI_worst"
)

if (late_AKI_valid) {
  outcomes_to_show <- c(
    "AKI_primary", "AKI_day56",
    "AKI_after6", "AKI_worst"
  )
}

outcome_summary <- eda %>%
  select(all_of(outcomes_to_show)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Outcome",
    values_to = "AKI"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Outcome) %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = sum(!is.na(AKI)),
    AKI_events = sum(AKI == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Proportion = fmt_pct(AKI_events, Patients),
    Outcome = outcome_labels[Outcome]
  )

knitr::kable(
  outcome_summary,
  caption = "AKI frequency under different outcome definitions"
)
```

```{r outcome-consistency-note, results='asis'}
if (late_AKI_valid) {
  cat(
    "**Outcome consistency:** No observed nesting violations. ",
    "The exploratory AKI-after-day-6 indicator was calculated ",
    "from the two existing outcomes."
  )
} else {
  cat(
    "**Outcome consistency warning:** ",
    nesting_errors,
    " patient(s) have AKI on days 5-6 without primary AKI. ",
    "The AKI-after-day-6 outcome has therefore been excluded."
  )
}
```

# Missing Data

```{r missing-data}
missing_data <- data %>%
  summarise(
    across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x)))
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Missing_n"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Missing_percent = round(
      100 * Missing_n / nrow(data), 1
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Missing_n))

missing_present <- missing_data %>%
  filter(Missing_n > 0)

if (nrow(missing_present) > 0) {
  knitr::kable(
    missing_present,
    caption = "Variables containing missing observations"
  )
} else {
  cat("No missing values coded as NA were found.")
}
```

```{r missing-plot, fig.height=4.5}
if (nrow(missing_present) > 0) {

  p_missing <- ggplot(
    missing_present,
    aes(
      x = reorder(Variable, Missing_percent),
      y = Missing_percent
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(fill = grey, width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(
        "n = ", Missing_n,
        " (", Missing_percent, "%)"
      )),
      hjust = -0.1,
      size = 3.3
    ) +
    coord_flip(clip = "off") +
    scale_y_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.35))
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Missing Values by Variable",
      x = NULL,
      y = "Missing observations (%)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

  print(p_missing)
}
```

# Observed AKI by Artificial Protein Intake

This comparison includes the primary, secondary, worst-case, and—if valid—derived late AKI outcomes.

For comparability, patients must have nonmissing protein intake and all three original AKI outcomes.




```{r outcome-protein-plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=6}

# ============================================================
# OBSERVED AKI BY ARTIFICIAL PROTEIN INTAKE
# Four outcome definitions
# ============================================================

# 1. Prepare the data
aki_plot_data <- data %>%
  transmute(
    Protein = as.numeric(Protein_intake__d1_4),
    AKI_primary = as.numeric(AKI_any),
    AKI_day56 = as.numeric(AKI_any_early),
    AKI_worst = as.numeric(
      AKI_any_sensitivity_worst_case
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Protein_group = factor(
      case_when(
        Protein == 0 ~ "Zero",
        Protein > 0 ~ "Positive",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
      ),
      levels = c("Zero", "Positive")
    )
  )

# 2. Verify outcome consistency
# AKI on days 5-6 must also count as AKI after day 4
nesting_errors <- sum(
  aki_plot_data$AKI_day56 == 1 &
    aki_plot_data$AKI_primary == 0,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (nesting_errors > 0) {
  stop(
    "The AKI outcomes are inconsistent: ",
    nesting_errors,
    " patients have AKI on days 5-6 but ",
    "not AKI after day 4. ",
    "AKI after day 6 cannot be derived reliably."
  )
}

# 3. Derive AKI after day 6
aki_plot_data <- aki_plot_data %>%
  mutate(
    AKI_after6 = case_when(
      AKI_primary == 1 & AKI_day56 == 0 ~ 1L,
      AKI_primary == 1 & AKI_day56 == 1 ~ 0L,
      AKI_primary == 0 & AKI_day56 == 0 ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  )

# 4. Use the same patients for all four outcomes
aki_long <- aki_plot_data %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(Protein_group),
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(AKI_day56),
    !is.na(AKI_worst),
    !is.na(AKI_after6)
  ) %>%
  select(
    Protein_group,
    AKI_primary,
    AKI_day56,
    AKI_after6,
    AKI_worst
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -Protein_group,
    names_to = "Outcome",
    values_to = "AKI"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = factor(
      Outcome,
      levels = c(
        "AKI_primary",
        "AKI_day56",
        "AKI_after6",
        "AKI_worst"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "AKI after day 4",
        "AKI on days 5-6",
        "AKI after day 6",
        "Worst-case AKI"
      )
    )
  )

# 5. Calculate observed AKI proportions
aki_risk_summary <- aki_long %>%
  group_by(Outcome, Protein_group) %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    AKI_events = sum(AKI == 1),
    AKI_risk = mean(AKI == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Summary table
knitr::kable(
  aki_risk_summary %>%
    mutate(
      AKI_percent = round(100 * AKI_risk, 1)
    ) %>%
    select(
      Outcome,
      Protein_group,
      Patients,
      AKI_events,
      AKI_percent
    ),
  caption = "Observed AKI by artificial protein intake"
)

# 6. Create the four-panel plot
p_aki_comparison <- ggplot(
  aki_risk_summary,
  aes(
    x = Protein_group,
    y = AKI_risk,
    fill = Protein_group
  )
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        round(AKI_risk * 100, 1), "%",
        "\n(", AKI_events, "/", Patients, ")"
      )
    ),
    vjust = -0.3,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Outcome,
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Zero" = "#EF4444",
      "Positive" = "#3B82F6"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Zero", "Positive"),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::percent,
    breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, 1.1),
    clip = "off"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Observed AKI by Artificial Protein Intake",
    subtitle = "Comparison of AKI outcome definitions",
    x = "Artificial protein intake",
    y = "Observed AKI proportion"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )

print(p_aki_comparison)

```


These proportions are descriptive and unadjusted. The different AKI outcomes cover different observation periods or assumptions.

# Primary AKI by Oral Feeding Duration

The following figure displays five panels for oral-feeding duration (0–4 days). The sixth panel contains patient counts by protein group.



```{r oral-aki-grid, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.5}

# ============================================================
# PRIMARY AKI BY ARTIFICIAL PROTEIN AND ORAL FEEDING
# ICU DEATHS EXCLUDED
# ============================================================

# 1. Prepare surviving patients
aki_feeding_data <- eda %>%
  filter(
    ICU_death == 0,
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(Protein_group),
    !is.na(Oral_days),
    Oral_days %in% 0:4
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Oral_group = factor(Oral_days, levels = 0:4)
  )

# 2. Calculate AKI proportions
aki_feeding_risk <- aki_feeding_data %>%
  group_by(Oral_group, Protein_group) %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    AKI_events = sum(AKI_primary == 1),
    AKI_risk = mean(AKI_primary == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Count patients per group
patient_counts <- aki_feeding_data %>%
  count(Oral_group, Protein_group, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    Oral_group = factor(0:4, levels = 0:4),
    Protein_group = factor(
      c("Zero", "Positive"),
      levels = c("Zero", "Positive")
    ),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Protein_group,
    values_from = n
  ) %>%
  arrange(Oral_group) %>%
  mutate(Total = Zero + Positive)

# 4. Function to create individual AKI panels
make_aki_panel <- function(day) {

  panel_data <- aki_feeding_risk %>%
    filter(as.character(Oral_group) == as.character(day))

  ggplot(
    panel_data,
    aes(
      x = Protein_group,
      y = AKI_risk,
      fill = Protein_group
    )
  ) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(
        round(AKI_risk * 100, 1), "%",
        "\n(", AKI_events, "/", Patients, ")"
      )),
      vjust = -0.3,
      size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c(
        "Zero" = "#EF4444",
        "Positive" = "#3B82F6"
      ),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = c("Zero", "Positive"),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent,
      breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0, 1.12),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Oral feeding:", day, "days"),
      x = NULL,
      y = "AKI proportion"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(
        size = 11,
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
}

# 5. Create five AKI panels
aki_panels <- lapply(0:4, make_aki_panel)

# 6. Prepare patient-count table
table_data <- patient_counts %>%
  mutate(
    Day = as.integer(as.character(Oral_group)),
    y = 5 - Day
  ) %>%
  select(Day, y, Zero, Positive, Total) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Zero, Positive, Total),
    names_to = "Group",
    values_to = "Count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    x = match(Group, c("Zero", "Positive", "Total")) + 1
  )

# 7. Create patient-count table plot
p_table <- ggplot() +

  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = 0.5, xmax = 4.5,
    ymin = 5.5, ymax = 6.5,
    fill = "#E5E7EB"
  ) +

  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 1:4,
    y = 6,
    label = c("Oral days", "Zero", "Positive", "Total"),
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.1
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = table_data,
    aes(
      x = x,
      y = y,
      label = Count,
      color = Group
    ),
    size = 3.8,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +

  geom_text(
    data = data.frame(Day = 0:4),
    aes(
      x = 1,
      y = 5 - Day,
      label = Day
    ),
    size = 3.8
  ) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0.5:5.5,
    color = "#D1D5DB",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +

  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "Zero" = "#EF4444",
      "Positive" = "#3B82F6",
      "Total" = "#374151"
    )
  ) +

  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(0.5, 4.5),
    ylim = c(0.5, 6.5),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +

  labs(title = "Surviving Patients (n)") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

# 8. Combine all six panels
p_aki_feeding <- patchwork::wrap_plots(
  c(aki_panels, list(p_table)),
  ncol = 3
) +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "Primary AKI by Artificial Protein and Oral Feeding",
    subtitle = "ICU deaths excluded; observed AKI proportions among survivors"
  )

print(p_aki_feeding)

```


```{r aki-mortality-by-oral-feeding, fig.width=11, fig.height=5}

# ============================================================
# AKI AND ICU MORTALITY BY ORAL FEEDING DAYS
# ============================================================

# 1. AKI proportions among ICU survivors
aki_by_oral <- eda %>%
  filter(
    ICU_death == 0,
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(Oral_days),
    Oral_days %in% 0:4
  ) %>%
  group_by(Oral_days) %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    Events = sum(AKI_primary == 1),
    Proportion = Events / Patients,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Oral_days = factor(Oral_days, levels = 0:4)
  )

# 2. ICU mortality proportions among all patients
death_by_oral <- eda %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(ICU_death),
    !is.na(Oral_days),
    Oral_days %in% 0:4
  ) %>%
  group_by(Oral_days) %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    Events = sum(ICU_death == 1),
    Proportion = Events / Patients,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Oral_days = factor(Oral_days, levels = 0:4)
  )

# 3. Reusable function for the bar plots
make_proportion_plot <- function(plot_data, title, color) {

  ggplot(
    plot_data,
    aes(x = Oral_days, y = Proportion)
  ) +
    geom_col(
      fill = color,
      width = 0.65
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(
        round(Proportion * 100, 1), "%",
        "\n(", Events, "/", Patients, ")"
      )),
      vjust = -0.35,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(
      limits = as.character(0:4),
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      labels = scales::percent,
      breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.2)
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(
      ylim = c(0, 1.12),
      clip = "off"
    ) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      x = "Days of exclusively oral feeding",
      y = "Observed proportion"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 11
      )
    )
}

# 4. AKI plot
p_aki_oral <- make_proportion_plot(
  aki_by_oral,
  "AKI Among ICU Survivors",
  "#EF4444"
)

# 5. Mortality plot
p_death_oral <- make_proportion_plot(
  death_by_oral,
  "ICU Mortality (All Patients)",
  "#64748B"
)

# 6. Display side by side
p_aki_mortality <- p_aki_oral + p_death_oral +
  patchwork::plot_annotation(
    title = "AKI and ICU Mortality by Oral Feeding Duration",
    subtitle = "Bars display percentages and event counts / group size"
  )

print(p_aki_mortality)

```


# Mortality Sensitivity Analysis

The worst-case outcome reclassifies patients who died in the ICU without documented AKI as AKI cases.

This comparison identifies how many patients change classification.

```{r worst-case-comparison}
paired_data <- eda %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(AKI_primary),
    !is.na(AKI_worst)
  )

sensitivity_summary <- paired_data %>%
  summarise(
    Patients = n(),
    Primary_AKI = sum(AKI_primary == 1),
    Worst_case_AKI = sum(AKI_worst == 1),
    Reclassified_to_AKI = sum(
      AKI_primary == 0 & AKI_worst == 1
    ),
    Reclassified_from_AKI = sum(
      AKI_primary == 1 & AKI_worst == 0
    )
  )

knitr::kable(
  sensitivity_summary,
  caption = "Primary versus worst-case AKI classification"
)

# Verify that reclassified patients died in ICU
death_check <- paired_data %>%
  filter(
    AKI_primary == 0,
    AKI_worst == 1
  ) %>%
  count(ICU_death, name = "Patients") %>%
  mutate(
    Death_status = case_when(
      ICU_death == 1 ~ "Died in ICU",
      ICU_death == 0 ~ "Did not die in ICU",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(Death_status, Patients)

knitr::kable(
  death_check,
  caption = "Mortality among reclassified patients"
)
```

The worst-case analysis examines sensitivity to the handling of death. It does not establish that the reclassified patients actually developed AKI.

# Readiness for Regression Analysis

```{r model-readiness}
model_variables <- c(
  "AKI_any",
  "Protein_intake__d1_4",
  "EuroScore2",
  "BMI",
  "Duration_of_cardiopulmonary_bypass_minutes",
  "SBP"
)

complete_cases <- complete.cases(
  data[model_variables]
)

regression_readiness <- tibble::tibble(
  Measure = c(
    "Patients with complete model data",
    "AKI events in complete cases",
    "Non-AKI patients in complete cases"
  ),

  Count = c(
    sum(complete_cases),
    sum(data$AKI_any[complete_cases] == 1),
    sum(data$AKI_any[complete_cases] == 0)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  regression_readiness,
  caption = "Data availability for the candidate primary regression model"
)
```

# Conclusions and Next Steps

The exploratory analysis examines the distributions of artificial protein intake, AKI outcomes, oral-feeding duration, and selected clinical characteristics.

Key methodological considerations:

- **Confounding by indication:** Artificial protein administration was determined by the treating physician.
- **Exposure overlap:** Four days of exclusive oral feeding correspond to zero artificially administered protein.
- **Competing events:** In-ICU death can prevent subsequent AKI from being observed.
- **Outcome timing:** The primary, secondary, and derived late AKI outcomes cover different observation windows.
- **Observational interpretation:** Descriptive differences cannot establish a causal effect of protein intake.

The next stage is to specify a clinically justified adjustment set, fit the primary regression model, assess model assumptions, and perform the predefined secondary and mortality sensitivity analyses.
